data.content_ref: inline:The protocol asserts silent displacement is structurally impossible because evidence is content-addressed, but immutability of individual nodes does not causally prevent displacement: the target itself notes that the Merkle-DAG root pointer or naming index may still be mutable. The mechanism provides no durable record of evidence roots or workspace ancestry to anchor that index after a crash, so reclamation has no causal foothold to know which nodes are still reachable evidence and which are orphans. A silent update to the root pointer can therefore exclude completed evidence without altering the immutable nodes, violating the guarantee.
